Re: Draft Environmental Statement Proposed Endangered Species Conservation Act of 1972
Dear Mr. Hendricks:
The referenced environmental statement has been reviewed by the personnel of this division. This environmental statement provides for legislation to increase the authority of the Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife to purchase areas for the conservation, protection, and propagation of species and sub-species of fish and wildlife that might be threatened with extinction.
We are of the opinion that some consideration should be given and included in this statement that might provide protection from disease vectors that might be produced within these protective areas. It is suggested that the following comments be considered and added to the environmental statement:
1. Land acquired for the protection of endangered species must not be permitted to produce vectors of human disease or <u>nuisance</u> species that endanger the inhabitants of surrounding lands.
Where land alterations have been made by governmental agencies or individuals for the control of human disease vectors prior to acquisition, these alterations shall be maintained in such a manner that they will continue to control these vectors.
3. Where the acquired land creates conditions that result in the production of human disease vectors or prevents the normal development of adjacent land, the alteration of the acquired land shall be permitted in order to alleviate these conditions.
